A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MTA work, and all ten pages, including equations, figures, tables, and references, are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both mention separate supplementary materials that are unavailable for this comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MTA detection and captioning experiments, qualitative examples, and component, layer, and loss ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports InternLM2 comparisons and detection results stratified by object frequency, weather, and time of day.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same BLA and DCA components, alignment losses, prompt pooling, training objective, and inference procedure. Testing InternLM2 does not introduce a documented change to the MTA algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes and TOD3Cap for 3D detection and dense captioning. v2 Table 3 disaggregates the existing nuScenes validation population; it does not introduce additional data, tasks, or altered input conditions.

E2.justification: The comparator methods remain Scan2Cap, X-Trans2Cap, Vote2Cap-DETR, TOD3Cap, and BEVFormer in their respective comparisons. InternLM2 adds another configuration for TOD3Cap and MTA, rather than a new comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds an InternLM2 experimental configuration and evaluates mAP separately across frequency, weather, and time-of-day groups. The original Llama-3.2-1B setting, dataset splits, metrics, IoU thresholds, ten-epoch training budget, and learning rate remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 3 examines whether detection improvements persist for rare objects and different weather and lighting conditions. The existing component, attachment-layer, and alignment-loss ablations are unchanged, moving from Tables 3–6 to Tables 4–7; the qualitative example is also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. v2 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially extends the reported evidence with another language model and condition-specific detection results. The new InternLM2 comparison reports TOD3Cap/MTA CIDEr@0.5 of 105.1/113.0 and mAP of 26.8/27.6; Table 3 adds rare-object mAP of 17.1/18.9 and nighttime mAP of 12.4/13.1. Original Llama results and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives are equivalent. Changes to transpose notation, definition symbols, and caption-metric notation do not alter the mathematics; no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces its highlighted 4.9% overall perception improvement with a 10.7% improvement in rare perception scenarios. The introduction retains the overall 4.9% claim, while the central BLA/DCA contributions, captioning claim, and absence of additional inference overhead remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets the results as supporting effectiveness across language models and robust generalization to long-tail and nighttime conditions. Existing explanations of alignment mechanisms, hallucination reduction, and loss choices remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents pretrained InternLM2 as an alternative and specifies Llama 3 as the default configuration. Table 3 supplies rare/common/frequent thresholds of below 2%, 2–20%, and above 20%. Existing training details are retained; the V100 timing disclosure moves from the Table 2 caption into the complexity discussion.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the InternLM2 Technical Report, BEVDiffuser, and Position: Prospective of Autonomous Driving, while removing Driving with LLMs. The related-work organization and positioning around joint perception-captioning alignment remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and wording corrections, revises experimental discussion, and introduces a labeled Computational Complexity paragraph. Jingru Luo is added to the author list. The section sequence and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain language-model columns, additional rows, and grouped headers; a new Table 3 is inserted. Existing ablation tables gain Captioning/Perception group headings and are repositioned. Figure 2 is reduced in size, but its content and the framework diagram remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional language-model comparisons and condition-specific analysis provide useful support for portability and robustness beyond v1's single-model, aggregate evaluation. These are limited extensions of otherwise unchanged evidence. A small reporting inconsistency remains: the text gives rare/nighttime gains of 10.7%/5.7%, whereas Table 3's caption gives 10.5%/5.6%. Overall, the added evidence modestly improves the paper.
